name: נגזרת של ((1−xⁿ)/(1+xⁿ)) בחזקה שברית (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:

\( \displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\left({{CT:1}}\right)^{{CT:2}}\right] = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write the function as a power of an inner function \(g\); differentiate \(g\) with the quotient rule and the power with the chain rule, then multiply.
Step 1 — The chain rule
To solve this problem you will need to use the chain rule and the quotient rule.
The chain rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\,g'(x) \)
The quotient rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2} \)
Let

\[ f({{CT:0}})={{CT:3}} \]

and

\[ g({{CT:0}})={{CT:1}}. \]

Then \(f({{CT:0}})=[g({{CT:0}})]^{{CT:2}}\). So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:3}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{dx} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}]\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[g] \end{array} \]

Step 2 — The inner function: the quotient rule
In order to find \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you have to define two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:4}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:5}}\). So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}(g) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left(\frac{h}{i}\right) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i - h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}}{i^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:4}})\right]\cdot ({{CT:5}}) - ({{CT:4}})\cdot \left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:5}})\right]}{({{CT:5}})^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{[{{CT:6}}]\cdot ({{CT:5}}) - ({{CT:4}})\cdot [{{CT:7}}]}{{CT:8}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:8}}. \end{array} \]

Step 3 — The outer function
Now,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:2}}g^{{CT:10}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:11}} \end{array} \]

Step 4 — Putting it together
Hence,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:3}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}[g^{{CT:2}}]\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[g] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:8}}\cdot {{CT:11}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:12}} \end{array} \]
